## Why This Is Asked
Tests bridging of callback-based C APIs with CGO, memory ownership of C strings, and returning a Go slice from C callbacks. It also touches concurrency safety when enumerating in parallel.

## Key Concepts
- CGO callbacks and //export
- cgo.Handle for passing Go values to C
- Go string conversion via C.GoString
- Memory ownership and lifecycle across language boundaries
- Synchronization and runtime.KeepAlive during callbacks

## Code Example
```c
// header
typedef struct { int id; const char* name; double value; } item_t;
typedef int (*enum_cb)(const item_t* item, void* user);
int enumerate_items(enum_cb cb, void* user);
```
```c
// minimal C implementation sketch
static int cb_wrapper(const item_t* item, void* user) { return 0; }
```
```go
//export go_item_cb
func go_item_cb(item *C.item_t, user unsafe.Pointer) C.int { /* convert and append to slice */ return 0 }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle errors from enumerate_items?
- How to scale for thousands of items or streaming data?
- How to cancel enumeration safely from Go side?
